introduction: HUSKY Health includes Connecticut Medicaid and CHIP coverage. The correct application route depends on which coverage group fits the applicant.
description: HUSKY Health includes Connecticut Medicaid and CHIP coverage. The correct application route depends on which coverage group fits the applicant.

sections.who: HUSKY A serves eligible children, parents, caregivers and pregnant applicants; HUSKY B is CHIP for eligible uninsured children. HUSKY C covers qualifying older, blind or disabled residents, while HUSKY D serves eligible adults without dependent children.
sections.get: Coverage can help with medical care and other covered services. HUSKY B may involve family cost sharing; do not assume every HUSKY pathway has identical rules.
sections.docs:

sections.apply:
1. Choose the application route

    Use Access Health CT for HUSKY A, B or D.

  2. Use ConneCT for HUSKY C

    Applicants for HUSKY C or Medicaid for Employees with Disabilities can use ConneCT, under Apply for Benefits.

  3. Respond to the determination

    Submit requested evidence and read the notice for each applicant. Different people in one household can qualify through different pathways.
sections.after: Update address and phone details so renewal notices reach you. If not eligible, ask about other coverage options rather than assuming an entire family is excluded.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using HUSKY coverage groups; DSS application routes. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is there one application website for everyone?
No. A, B and D use Access Health CT; C and MED-Connect use ConneCT.
It is Connecticut’s Children’s Health Insurance Program, with different income and cost-sharing rules.
What if I work and have a disability?
Ask DSS about MED-Connect rather than relying only on the ordinary HUSKY C limits.
Can members of a family have different coverage?
Yes. Eligibility is assessed by the relevant pathway for each person.
